name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent André Carson running with a large cash advantage
Prediction markets price Carson near 97% to win
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Carson holds a heavily Democratic Indianapolis seat with incumbency, a six-figure war chest, and markets pricing him around 96-97%, while the Republican has shown no fundraising. Fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A surprise Carson retirement or scandal, or a late-funded Republican challenger, would be the main way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
André Carson seeks another term in this Indianapolis-based district, one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in Indiana. He enters with the advantages of incumbency, more than $1 million raised this cycle, and over $600,000 in cash on hand. Republican Patrick McAuley has no reported fundraising, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public general-election polling exists for the race, but prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Carson's chances at roughly 96 to 97 percent. The district's strong partisan lean and the challenger's lack of visible resources make an upset highly unlikely.
